categories.label: Letting agent and management fees
categories.tooltip: Fees you pay an agent to find tenants, collect rent or manage the property.

categories.label: Repairs and maintenance
categories.tooltip: Work that puts the property back to how it was, such as fixing a boiler or repainting. Improvements and extensions do not count.

categories.label: Landlord insurance
categories.tooltip: Buildings, contents and rent guarantee insurance for the let property.

categories.label: Council tax and utilities you pay
categories.tooltip: Council tax, gas, electricity and water you pay for the let property, not bills your tenant pays.

categories.label: Ground rent and service charges
categories.tooltip: Ground rent and service charges on a leasehold property you let out.

categories.label: Accountancy fees
categories.tooltip: Fees for preparing your property accounts and the property pages of your tax return.

categories.label: Replacing furniture and appliances
categories.tooltip: Replacing a sofa, fridge or carpet like for like, minus anything you got for the old one. First purchases do not count.

categories.label: Legal and professional fees
categories.tooltip: Fees for lets of a year or less, renewing a lease under 50 years, or chasing unpaid rent. Buying costs do not count.

categories.label: Travel to the property
categories.tooltip: Journeys you make only to visit, inspect or repair the let property.

categories.label: Advertising for tenants
categories.tooltip: Listing fees, adverts and photographs used to find new tenants.
